title: How do we write six fractions as mixed numbers?
description: Each fraction is split into the wholes it holds and the parts left over. The board finds the wholes by counting groups of the bottom number, keeps the leftover as a fraction and checks by multiplying back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the whole number counts the groups of the bottom number, and the fraction holds what is left. Watch for students who change the bottom number of the leftover fraction.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (section 7.5, second block)
video_script.why: A learner writes fractions greater than one as mixed numbers by taking out groups of the bottom number.
video_script.substitution: the book's own six fractions, with nine halves worked like the rest
video_script.anchor: six fractions written in a list on the board
video_script.payoff_line: All six fractions are written as mixed numbers

final_answer.spoken: nine halves is four and one half, nine fifths is one and four fifths, twenty one nineteenths is one and two nineteenths, forty seven ninths is five and two ninths, twelve elevenths is one and one eleventh, and nineteen sixths is three and one sixth

video_script.fraction_reading: nine halves, nine fifths, twenty one nineteenths, forty seven ninths, twelve elevenths, nineteen sixths
maths_rules: check: whole x bottom + leftover = top
video_script.design: Each fraction is split into groups of its bottom number, which become whole bars, and a leftover that stays as a fraction.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the six fractions 9/2, 9/5, 21/19, 47/9, 12/11 and 19/6 in a list; the words mixed number beside a whole number and a fraction

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.list: the six fractions are written in a list
marks.def: a whole number and a fraction are written side by side and labelled mixed number
marks.ask: the question is written below the list

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about six fractions.
<bookmark mark='list'/>They are nine halves, nine fifths, twenty one nineteenths, forty seven ninths, twelve elevenths and nineteen sixths.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A whole number with a fraction beside it is called a mixed number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we write each fraction as a mixed number?

beats.on_screen: the list of fractions stays; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a whole unit bar beside the bottom number of equal parts, for example two halves or five fifths

marks.count: a whole unit bar is shown filled by as many parts as the bottom number says

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>To find the whole number, count how many wholes the fraction holds.
Each whole needs as many parts as the bottom number says.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six fractions, each with a top number bigger than its bottom number.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction as a mixed number
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction as a whole number and a fraction.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 9 = 4 x 2 + 1, so 9/2 = 4 wholes and 1/2 left; 9 = 1 x 5 + 4, so 9/5 = 1 whole and 4/5 left

marks.half: nine halves is split into four groups of two halves
marks.fifth: nine fifths is split into one group of five fifths and four fifths

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step one, we use the same way as the examples in your book. Nine halves holds four wholes, because four groups of two make eight.
<bookmark mark='halfleft'/>One half is left over.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>Nine fifths holds one whole, because one group of five fits in nine. Four fifths are left over.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 21 = 1 x 19 + 2, so 21/19 = 1 whole and 2/19 left; 47 = 5 x 9 + 2, so 47/9 = 5 wholes and 2/9 left

marks.nine: twenty one nineteenths is split into one group of nineteen and two nineteenths
marks.ninths: forty seven ninths is split into five groups of nine and two ninths

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, twenty one nineteenths holds one whole, and two nineteenths are left over.
<bookmark mark='ninths'/>Forty seven ninths holds five wholes, because five groups of nine make forty five. Two ninths are left over.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 12 = 1 x 11 + 1, so 12/11 = 1 whole and 1/11 left; 19 = 3 x 6 + 1, so 19/6 = 3 wholes and 1/6 left

marks.eleven: twelve elevenths is split into one group of eleven and one eleventh
marks.sixths: nineteen sixths is split into three groups of six and one sixth

narration: <bookmark mark='eleven'/>Step three, twelve elevenths holds one whole, and one eleventh is left over.
<bookmark mark='sixths'/>Nineteen sixths holds three wholes, because three groups of six make eighteen. One sixth is left over.

beats.on_screen: Check: whole x bottom + left over = top; 4 x 2 + 1 = 9, 1 x 5 + 4 = 9, 1 x 19 + 2 = 21, 5 x 9 + 2 = 47, 1 x 11 + 1 = 12, 3 x 6 + 1 = 19

marks.rule: the rule whole times bottom plus leftover equals top is written
marks.first: the first three checks are written
marks.last: the last three checks are written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>To check, multiply the whole number by the bottom number and add the left over.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four times two plus one is nine. One times five plus four is nine. One times nineteen plus two is twenty one.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Five times nine plus two is forty seven. One times eleven plus one is twelve. Three times six plus one is nineteen.

marks.first: the first three answers are read
marks.last: the last three answers are read

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All six fractions are written as mixed numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Nine halves is four and one half. Nine fifths is one and four fifths. Twenty one nineteenths is one and two nineteenths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Forty seven ninths is five and two ninths. Twelve elevenths is one and one eleventh. Nineteen sixths is three and one sixth.
